diagnosis: HBV calibrated with DDS on NSE over 1971-10 to 1997-12 (after a 1-year warm-up). The best set gives NSE 0.63, KGE 0.74, PBIAS -1.3% and r 0.79. A second DDS run started from different parameters reached a similar but slightly worse optimum (NSE 0.613), with the same FC (about 126 mm), a low BETA and a warm TT. The response surface therefore looks fairly consistent. Final parameters: FC 126, LP 0.84, BETA 0.79, a fast and flashy response (K0 0.67, K1 0.57, UZL 23, MAXBAS 2.6), a moderate baseflow (K2 0.086, PERC 3.8), TT 1.4, CFMAX 3.9 and SFCF 0.86. This fits a steep, upland catchment with peaty shrub cover and little groundwater. Weaknesses: daily NSE is limited (about 0.63). The model probably underestimates the highest flood peaks and gets their timing wrong, because rainfall over a large upland catchment is uncertain and the routing is lumped. Snow storage and melt (CFR and CWH at their lower bounds, TT above 0) are poorly identified and could mis-time spring melt peaks. I'm moderately confident in the water balance and recession parameters, less so in the snow and peak-routing parameters. I expect NSE of about 0.55-0.65 in the independent period.
